package.description: Maintained aria2 fork with extensive bug fixes and modernized architecture

en-US.author: AnInsomniac
en-US.description: Maintained aria2 fork with extensive bug fixes and modernized architecture
en-US.longDescription:
aria2 is remarkable open source software. For over a decade it has been one of the most capable
download engines available, trusted by countless tools and users worldwide. We are deeply grateful
to the original authors and contributors of the aria2 project. They built something that has stood
the test of time, and that enduring quality is the best testament to their vision and craftsmanship.

But upstream development has slowed dramatically in recent years. Dependencies grew stale, builds
broke on modern platforms, and a backlog of bugs went unaddressed. We picked up the baton: migrated
the codebase to a modern build framework, triaged and fixed a substantial number of upstream issues,
and introduced ED2K protocol support for the first time. A full audit trail is preserved in
docs/maintenance/upstream-issue-review/matrix.csv.

Aria2 Next is an actively maintained aria2-compatible engine for everyone, and it is also the embedded
engine used by Motrix Next. Original interfaces, including options, configuration, sessions, JSON-RPC,
and libaria2, remain intact so downstream projects get a seamless upgrade. The focus is straightforward:
release reliability, current dependency baselines, and ongoing compatibility fixes. Same engine, renewed
foundation.
en-US.name: Aria2 Next
en-US.releaseNotes:
## Summary

Aria2 Next 3.0.9 makes HTTP downloads more reliable and faster on poor routes. A retried download no longer corrupts its file. A slow connection no longer holds back the end of a download. A broken IPv6 route no longer keeps a download at a crawl. Release assets cover the same seven platforms.

### Fixed

• A download retried after a failure no longer treats the unwritten part of its preallocated file as received. With `--continue`, the retry resumes from the ranges the earlier attempt actually wrote ([rayburst#767](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/767)).
• A server that answers HTTP 403 to additional connections while others are transferring now limits the connection count instead of failing the download. The count is probed upward again later ([rayburst#767](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/767)).
• The end of a download no longer slows to a crawl behind one slow connection. Its remaining range is handed to idle connections, which take over the part the slow connection would deliver last ([rayburst#762](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/762)).
• When one address family is several times slower per connection than the other, existing connections move to the faster one. Previously only new connections switched, so a slow IPv6 route could hold every connection of a download. In testing, a 156 MB download that took 26 to 120 seconds over such a route finished in 6 to 9 seconds.
• A connection that stays far slower than the others for several seconds is replaced by a new one. Replacements back off when the new connection is no faster.
• Progress is printed again when the output is not a console, such as under Scoop. A download shorter than a second still gets a progress line ([#70](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/issues/70)).
• A paused multi-file torrent resumes without asking for its file selection again ([rayburst#754](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/754)).
• Session files saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark, as Windows editors and PowerShell 5 write them, load correctly.

### Added

• [`docs/rpc-extensions.md`](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/blob/v3.0.9/docs/rpc-extensions.md) documents the RPC fields and methods added beyond aria2's interface ([#76](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/issues/76)).

### Downloads

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | `aria2-next-3.0.9-linux-x86_64` |
| Linux ARM64 | `aria2-next-3.0.9-linux-aarch64` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `aria2-next-3.0.9-macos-arm64` |
| macOS Intel | `aria2-next-3.0.9-macos-x86_64` |
| Windows x86_64 | `aria2-next-3.0.9-windows-x86_64.exe` |
| Windows ARM64 | `aria2-next-3.0.9-windows-arm64.exe` |
| Android ARM64 | `aria2-next-3.0.9-android-arm64` |
| Checksums | `aria2-next-3.0.9-checksums.sha256` |
